input: Write a one-page business plan for my consulting idea

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Consulting spans wildly different fields — the industry or domain shapes every section of the plan, from the problem statement to the competitive landscape.
Knowing who the target clients are determines the value proposition, pricing model, and how services are positioned.
Whether this is a solo practice, a small team, or a side venture changes the scale, resource assumptions, and feasibility claims in the plan.
A startup with no budget needs a lean, bootstrapped plan; one with funding can project hiring and marketing spend — this changes the financial section entirely.
The intended audience — investor, bank, personal reference, or accelerator — dictates the tone, level of formality, and which sections to emphasise.
The user may define success as acquiring first clients, reaching a revenue milestone, or simply having a clear personal roadmap — this shapes what the plan must prove.
The desired output format (Word doc, PDF, structured sections, narrative prose) and how soon it is needed affects how the plan is structured and delivered.

gold.taskTitle: Write a one-page business plan for consulting
gold.taskDescription: Draft a concise, one-page business plan for the user's consulting business idea.

questions.title: What industry or field is your consulting focused on?
questions.description: Identify the specific domain (e.g., HR, finance, marketing, tech, operations) so the plan reflects relevant terminology, competitors, and market context.

questions.title: Who are the clients you want to serve?
questions.description: Define the target client profile — e.g., small businesses, startups, enterprise teams, non-profits — to shape the value proposition and positioning.

questions.title: Will you be working solo or with a team?
questions.description: Clarify the operating structure of the consultancy to accurately reflect capacity, delivery model, and resource assumptions in the plan.

questions.title: Do you have a starting budget or existing resources?
questions.description: Understand the financial baseline so the plan's projections and cost assumptions are realistic and grounded.

questions.title: Who will read this business plan — investor, bank, or yourself?
questions.description: Determine the intended audience to calibrate the tone, formality, and which sections (e.g., financials vs. vision) deserve the most emphasis.

questions.title: What does success look like in the first 12 months?
questions.description: Capture the user's primary goal — first client signed, a revenue target, a number of projects — so the plan builds toward a concrete, measurable outcome.

questions.title: What format or template do you need the plan in?
questions.description: Confirm the preferred output — narrative paragraphs, structured sections, a specific template, or a ready-to-share document — and any deadline for completion.
